summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican called St. Louis the fistic centre of the nation, home to champions Allen, Gallagher and McCoole, and on the eve of the Allen-Gallagher fight visited their saloons, starting with Allen's English-crowded Concert Saloon.

metadata.notes: masthead reads THE MISSOURI REPUBLICAN--ST. LOUIS, AUGUST 17, 1869

facts.fact: Allen ran a "Concert Saloon" on Fifth Street between Biddle and O'Fallon streets, with a bar in front and a back room with tables and a piano on a platform; its patrons were mostly English
places: Fifth Street between Biddle and O'Fallon, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen, Charley Gallagher and Mike McCoole were all permanent residents of St. Louis, each keeping a saloon
On the eve of the Allen-Gallagher fight, Allen and Gallagher planned to stay out of sight and join the excursion steamer at some point beyond St. Louis

notes: Most of the article is general color about St. Louis prize-fighting and the saloons of Gallagher, McCoole and Billy Carroll; Allen's saloon gets one section.
